results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response:
The major subdivisions of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system, as recorded in VFB. VFB describes the mushroom body as divided into: the calyx, which is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, which is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages. 

VFB holds various data related to the mushroom body, including images, neurons with some part in the mushroom body, neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body, parts of the mushroom body, and lineage clones found in the mushroom body. For more specific information, you can explore the available data, such as listing all available images of mushroom body, or viewing the neurons with some part in mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The LPLC2 visual neuron type is a type of neuron with specific characteristics and functions, as described in the VFB database. According to VFB, the cell body of LPLC2 lies in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind. It has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer, allowing it to detect looming stimuli. In the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. The arbors of LPLC2 span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells. LPLC2 projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. Its activity elicits a jump escape response. VFB records show that there are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe and they are cholinergic. VFB does not currently hold comprehensive data on all connections of LPLC2, but it is known to project to the PVLP.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, with a unique anatomy and connectivity profile. According to VFB, it has a distinct anatomy, with a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, and a large descending axon that enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. The giant fiber neuron has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. 

In terms of connectivity, the giant fiber neuron forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge and at the axonal lateral bend. VFB holds [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream connectivity classes and [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream connectivity classes for the giant fiber neuron. 

Available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron include [P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0121835FBtp0118557 "Open P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0116198FBtp0118471 "Open P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R14A01-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0122311FBtp0118233 "Open P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R14A01-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0122311FBtp0118471 "Open P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [P{VT004455-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R10A12-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0122730FBtp0118153 "Open P{VT004455-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R10A12-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain").

Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron include Phelan et al., 1996, King and Wyman, 1980, Stürner et al., 2025, Dorkenwald et al., 2024, Namiki et al., 2018, Thomas and Wyman, 1984, Koto et al., 1981, Power, 1948, Ito et al., 2014, Kamikouchi et al., 2009, Kennedy and Broadie, 2018, Allen et al., 1998, Bacon and Strausfeld, 1986, Matsuo et al., 2016, and Kim et al., 2020.

VFB holds [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of the giant fiber neuron, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting DNp01, [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") transgene expressions, and the aforementioned connectivity classes.

Similarly, for [neuron 2232 (FANC:492501)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_001027ke "Open neuron 2232 (FANC:492501) in Virtual Fly Brain"), VFB has annotated data on Neurons with similar morphology to neuron 2232 (FANC:492501) using the NBLAST algorithm, and the count of such neurons can be retrieved by running the relevant query. results.question: Is there a circuit diagram of the mushroom body available on Virtual Fly Brain?
results.response: According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, there are circuit diagrams and images of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") available. VFB holds [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of mushroom body") records of available images of the mushroom body. Additionally, VFB has annotated a large number of neurons related to the mushroom body, including [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, as well as parts of the mushroom body and tracts/nerves innervating it. The user can explore these data further by querying the available images, neurons, and parts of the mushroom body.
